request.deadline: Contract year covering 2026-2027; IOG contract stated as closing August 31, 2026; architecture assessment by Q3 2027
deliverables: Protocol maintenance including cardano-node and cardano-wallet upgrades, hard fork readiness, platform support, release engineering, and security/dependency maintenance
Compatible Daedalus release at least 2 weeks before each mainnet hard fork
Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support in a stable release
CIP-30 dApp connector in Daedalus with documentation and verified interoperability
Ongoing user support including Japanese-language support and full Japanese translation for new features
Architecture assessment published publicly by Q3 2027
Independent financial audit and milestone-based oversight through Intersect
request.recipient: Se7en Labs, Inc. with Intersect serving as administrator and milestone verifier
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Daedalus Wallet Maintenance and Improvements 2026-2027 as a time-and-materials engagement delivered by Se7en Labs, Inc.

claims.claim: Daedalus is Cardano's only full-node desktop wallet and derives wallet and governance data directly from the chain without third-party APIs or trusted backends.
Daedalus private keys are generated and stored on the user's device and are never transmitted to an external service, with open-source Apache 2.0 code allowing auditability.
Opt-in telemetry shows approximately 4,000 monthly active Daedalus users, while the proposer asserts the true count is meaningfully higher.

Se7en Labs assumed responsibility for Daedalus under an IOG contract in January 2026 and shipped Mithril bootstrap, UTxO-HD/LSM backend integration, Apple Silicon builds, a release CLI, Nix modernization, and Daedalus 8.0 and 11.0.
The proposal commits to stable Daedalus releases at least 2 weeks before each mainnet hard fork and to keeping cardano-node no more than 2 major versions behind the mainnet recommendation.
The work includes Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support, a CIP-30 dApp connector, Japanese localisation, user support, and a public architecture assessment.
The requested budget is 1,785,333 ADA, consisting of 1,666,667 ADA for labor, 33,333 ADA for test hardware, 33,333 ADA for financial audit, and a 52,000 ADA Intersect administration fee.
Any unspent labor, test hardware, or audit budget at contract close is to be returned to the treasury.

Intersect will administer funds, verify milestones, authorize monthly time-and-materials disbursements, hold funds in a dedicated auditable account, and use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with external oversight entities.
The proposer states the withdrawal does not breach the 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission and links to the relevant governance action.

summary: The document requests 1,785,333 ADA for a public-good maintenance and improvement program for Daedalus, emphasizing protocol compatibility, wallet security, open-source auditability, hardware wallet and CIP-30 support, Japanese localisation, and Intersect-administered milestone oversight.
